NDIA-ICT-INF-001
1. Purpose, governance and risk accountability
Infrastructure governance, risk appetite and reporting

NDIA must govern ICT infrastructure through approved accountable roles, risk appetite, internal controls and executive reporting so infrastructure decisions protect participant outcomes, support lawful collaboration, and keep security, availability, cost and lifecycle risks within approved tolerance.
Applies to all ICT infrastructure services, platforms and lifecycle decisions.

NDIA-ICT-INF-002
2. Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset control
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology

NDIA must manage each infrastructure system and asset through an ISM-aligned lifecycle from planning and procurement to operation, change and disposal; systems must be authorised or reauthorised before production or material change, recorded in asset and authorised-system registers, comply with applicable Commonwealth technology standards, and restrict prohibited, legacy, smart and IoT technologies unless risk-approved.
Applies to hardware, network, cloud, internet-facing, legacy, smart and IoT infrastructure assets.

3. Procurement, supplier assurance and contract security
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit

NDIA must procure and manage infrastructure suppliers through risk-based security, privacy, FOCI and financial approval checks; contracts must flow down PSPF, ISM and NDIA security obligations, require assurance evidence and audit rights, control subcontractors, and include monitored service, transition, exit, data return and secure disposal requirements.
Applies to infrastructure procurements, providers, contractors, subcontractors, managed services and renewals.

NDIA-ICT-INF-004
4. Cloud, hosting, data centre and service management
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit

NDIA cloud, hosting, gateway-hosting and data centre services must use approved government patterns, HCF-certified or otherwise risk-approved providers, current IRAP or required accreditation evidence, defined owners and service levels, approved data residency, portability, monitoring, reliability, cost and exit arrangements before and throughout production use.
Applies to cloud, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, hosting, data centre and provider-managed infrastructure services.

5. Information classification, privacy and protected information handling
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows

NDIA infrastructure must identify the classification, caveat, sensitivity and business impact of information it stores, processes or transmits, apply protective markings and metadata where required, and enforce approved access, storage, transmission, disclosure, offshore-access, privacy-governance, PIA and training controls for personal and protected NDIS information.
Applies to security classified, caveated, personal and protected NDIS information across hardware, network and cloud services.

6. Records, retention, FOI, migration and secure disposal
Commonwealth records, legal holds, retrieval, decommissioning and media sanitisation

NDIA infrastructure must create, preserve, retrieve and export required Commonwealth records, logs, metadata and service records; deletion, migration, cloud exit, sanitisation, destruction, de-identification or disposal of data, media and assets must occur only under approved retention, FOI, legal hold, Archives Act, privacy and ISM processes, with evidence retained.
Applies to records, datasets, logs, metadata, backups, hardware, media, provider records and decommissioning activities.

7. Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight, backups and cryptography
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls

NDIA infrastructure must implement the approved cyber security strategy, ISM controls and Essential Eight target maturity, including timely patching, application control, macro restrictions, user application hardening, protected and tested backups, relevant ASD mitigation strategies, and approved cryptography including post-quantum requirements where applicable.
Applies to endpoints, servers, network appliances, cloud workloads, administration endpoints and supporting infrastructure platforms.

8. Network, gateway, DNS and boundary security
Gateway/SSE, Protective DNS, segmentation and security visibility

NDIA networks and internet-connected infrastructure must use approved gateway, Secure Service Edge, Protective DNS or equivalent boundary controls; gateway services must be authorised, appropriately assessed, supply-chain assured, hosted, monitored, logged, vulnerability-managed and continuously tested commensurate with the information they protect.
Applies to internet-facing services, trusted/untrusted network boundaries, remote-access gateways, web proxies, mail relays, recursive resolvers and cloud gateway services.

Applies to user access, administrator access, privileged accounts, remote work, international administration, management consoles, physical access tokens and facility access.

Facilities, security zones, racks, access controls and surveillance protection

Applies to ICT facilities, data rooms, Security Zones One to Five, SCIFs, classified storage, racks, cabinets, media stores and supporting physical infrastructure.

Applies to security incidents, supplier incidents, privacy incidents, suspected fraud or corruption, cyber extortion events and external cyber coordination.

13. Fraud, corruption and misuse controls
Fraud risk assessment, preventive controls, detection and asset accountability

NDIA infrastructure governance must prevent, detect and respond to fraud, corruption and misuse through activity risk assessments, control plans, separation of duties, monitoring of billing, usage, inventory and privileged activity, and complete records of hardware movements, losses, returns and disposals.
Applies to infrastructure procurement, consumption, access administration, inventory, asset handling and disposal processes.

SOCI, Systems of Government Significance and critical data services

Where SOCI, Systems of Government Significance or critical-data obligations may apply, NDIA must assess triggers before infrastructure or provider changes, confirm provider regulatory status, issue required notifications, apply risk program and enhanced cyber obligations, protect regulated information, and maintain executive, legal and security escalation for incident or government assistance obligations.
Applies conditionally where SOCI, Systems of Government Significance, critical data storage or processing, or regulated provider obligations may be triggered.
